turns.text: Deadlines are better taken from the structured obligations than from prose, so I will start there.
Four separate remittances, one shared date. Confirming the date section, and checking what else a first hire brings with it.

Four monthly remittances, all due on the same day.

PAYE deducted from each salary (DOC-PAY-01#S1). Statutory health insurance contributions (DOC-PAY-01#S2). Statutory pension contributions (DOC-PAY-01#S3). The housing levy (DOC-PAY-01#S4).

All four are due by the 9th of the following month, so March payroll is remitted by 9 April (DOC-PAY-01#S5). They are four separate filings to different bodies even though they share a date, which is the part that usually catches people out in the first couple of months.

One thing that comes with hiring and is not a payroll remittance: you need written contracts, within 3 months of engagement, and employment records kept alongside them (DOC-EMP-01#S1, DOC-EMP-01#S2).

This corpus is synthetic and written for a software demonstration, so it is not legal advice.
